faq.description: A few things to know before we build your mobile app.

items.question: Do you build for both iOS and Android?
items.answer: Native and cross-platform development are available. The approach is chosen around your features, device requirements and maintenance needs.

items.question: Can the app connect to my existing systems?
items.answer: Apps can connect to existing back ends, payment providers and business tools through APIs. Access, compatibility and security are reviewed first.

items.question: What is involved in publishing an app?
items.answer: Launch planning includes store assets, testing and submission preparation. Developer accounts are required, and approval is controlled by Apple and Google.

items.question: How are updates and maintenance handled?
items.answer: Support can cover bug fixes, operating-system updates and new features. Coverage, response times and any ongoing costs are agreed separately.

hero.heading:
SaaS App
Development
hero.description: Scalable cloud software built around your business.

steps.title: Define the product
steps.description: Prioritize user needs, core features and the SaaS roadmap.

steps.title: Design the platform
steps.description: Plan user journeys, product screens and architecture.

steps.title: Build & integrate
steps.description: Develop the platform, subscriptions and essential integrations.

steps.title: Launch & scale
steps.description: Test, release and improve the product as usage grows.

faq.description: A few things to know before we build your SaaS platform.

items.question: Can we start with an MVP?
items.answer: An MVP focuses on the essential user journey and core features. Priorities are defined first so the product can be tested before broader investment.

items.question: Can you add subscriptions and user roles?
items.answer: Subscription billing, account management and role-based access can be included. Plans, permissions and payment-provider requirements are scoped together.

items.question: How do you plan for growth and data security?
items.answer: Architecture is shaped around expected usage, tenant separation and data sensitivity. Hosting, access controls, backups and monitoring are defined for the project.

items.question: Can the platform evolve after launch?
items.answer: New features, integrations and performance improvements can be planned in stages. Ongoing maintenance and development are covered by an agreed support scope.

steps.title: Map conversations
steps.description: Identify customer questions, journeys and automation goals.

steps.title: Design the flows
steps.description: Plan replies, decision paths and human handoffs.

steps.title: Connect & automate
steps.description: Set up WhatsApp workflows and integrate your tools.

steps.title: Test & optimize
steps.description: Validate conversations and refine the customer experience.

faq.description: A few things to know before automating your conversations.

items.question: What can WhatsApp automation help with?
items.answer: Common workflows include instant replies, lead qualification, product enquiries and order updates. The setup is tailored to your customer journey.

items.question: Do customers need to opt in to messages?
items.answer: Business-initiated messages require appropriate opt-in and must follow current WhatsApp policies. Approved templates may be required depending on the message type.

items.question: Can a team member take over from the chatbot?
items.answer: Agent handoff can be included for complex questions or customer requests. Routing rules and the tools your team uses are defined during setup.

items.question: Can it connect to my CRM, and are there extra fees?
items.answer: CRM and workflow integrations depend on available APIs. Meta, messaging-provider and third-party charges are separate considerations reviewed during scoping.

Design
hero.description: Intuitive digital experiences, shaped around users.

steps.title: Research & discover
steps.description: Understand user needs, business goals and pain points.

steps.title: Map & wireframe
steps.description: Define user flows and structure the key screens.

steps.title: Design & prototype
steps.description: Craft the visual interface and interactive prototype.

steps.title: Test & hand off
steps.description: Validate usability and prepare designs for development.

faq.description: A few things to know before we shape your user experience.

items.question: What is included in a UI/UX design project?
items.answer: The scope can include discovery, user flows, wireframes, interface design and prototypes. Deliverables are selected around your product and research needs.

items.question: Can you improve an existing website or app?
items.answer: An existing experience can be reviewed to identify usability issues. Priority journeys are then redesigned while keeping useful parts of the current product.

items.question: How is feedback included in the design process?
items.answer: Designs are reviewed at agreed milestones. Stakeholder feedback and, when included in scope, usability testing guide revisions before handoff.

items.question: What will the development team receive?
items.answer: Handoff can include editable Figma designs, reusable components, assets and interaction guidance. Responsive states and documentation are defined in the scope.

steps.title: Discover the brand
steps.description: Explore your values, audience and brand positioning.

steps.title: Shape the identity
steps.description: Develop the logo, color palette and typography.

steps.title: Build the brand kit
steps.description: Create consistent templates and essential brand assets.

steps.title: Deliver & guide
steps.description: Hand over the assets with clear brand usage guidelines.

faq.description: A few things to know before we create your brand kit.

items.question: What can a brand kit include?
items.answer: A kit can include logo variations, a color palette, typography, graphic elements and usage guidelines. Templates and stationery are defined in the scope.

items.question: Can you refresh an existing brand identity?
items.answer: An existing identity can be refined rather than replaced. Brand discovery helps decide which recognizable elements to keep and what needs to change.

items.question: Which asset formats will I receive?
items.answer: The handoff formats are agreed for your print and digital needs. These may include editable source artwork, SVG, PDF and transparent PNG exports.

items.question: How will my team use the brand consistently?
items.answer: Brand guidelines explain logo usage, colors, typography and common applications. Agreed templates help your team create consistent day-to-day materials.

steps.title: Set the strategy

steps.title: Create content
steps.description: Design branded graphics and write engaging social copy.

steps.title: Publish & engage
steps.description: Schedule posts and connect with your community.

steps.title: Measure & refine
steps.description: Review performance and improve the next content cycle.

faq.description: A few things to know before we plan your social content.

items.question: What does social media management include?
items.answer: The scope can cover strategy, content planning, branded graphics, captions and publishing. Community management and reporting can also be included.

items.question: Which platforms and posting frequency are covered?
items.answer: Platforms and publishing frequency are agreed around your audience, goals and available content. The content calendar sets out the planned deliverables.

items.question: Can I review content before it is published?
items.answer: An approval workflow can be set up so your team reviews planned copy and visuals. Review deadlines and revision rounds are agreed before publishing starts.

items.question: Are paid ads included, and how are results measured?
items.answer: Ad creative, campaign management and media spend are scoped separately. Reporting can track agreed measures such as reach, engagement, clicks and enquiries.

steps.title: Design the system
steps.description: Map user journeys, interfaces and the database structure.

steps.title: Build & integrate
steps.description: Develop the front end, APIs and connected back-end services.

steps.title: Test & deploy
steps.description: Validate performance, deploy and maintain your product.

faq.description: A few things to know before we build your full stack product.

items.question: What does full stack development cover?
items.answer: It connects the user interface, server-side logic, databases and APIs. Architecture, testing and deployment are planned as part of the agreed project scope.

items.question: Can you work with an existing application?
items.answer: An existing application can be assessed before extending or integrating it. Technical access and a review of the current architecture help define the approach.

items.question: How do you choose the technology stack?
items.answer: The stack is chosen around product requirements, integrations, expected scale and your team. Long-term maintainability and hosting needs also guide the decision.

items.question: How are security and deployment handled?
items.answer: Access controls, validation, testing and deployment workflows are designed for the application. Monitoring, backups and ongoing support are agreed during scoping.

steps.title: Discover & plan
steps.description: Understand your goals, audience and project requirements.

steps.title: Design the experience
steps.description: Create clear user journeys and a distinctive visual direction.

steps.title: Build & test
steps.description: Bring the design to life and check every key interaction.

steps.title: Launch & support
steps.description: Go live with confidence and keep your experience improving.

faq.description: A few things to know before we build your website.

items.question: What types of websites can you build?
items.answer: Custom web applications, responsive websites, e-commerce stores and landing pages. The right approach depends on your goals, content and integrations.

items.question: Will my website work on mobile devices?
items.answer: Responsive layouts adapt to mobile, tablet and desktop screens. Testing covers key devices, browsers and the journeys your visitors use most.

items.question: Can you connect a CMS or payment system?
items.answer: CMS platforms, payment providers and third-party APIs can be included. Compatibility, access and any provider fees are reviewed during scoping.

items.question: How are timelines and ongoing support planned?
items.answer: Timing depends on page count, features, content and feedback. Launch milestones and any maintenance or support arrangements are agreed in the project scope.
